headline: Coach strength drives growth, Tapestry raises outlook
summary_short: Tapestry's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 21% y/y to $1.92B on Coach strength (+31%), with GAAP diluted EPS up 74% y/y to $1.65 and operating margin expanding 630bps to 22.3%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 21% y/y (25% pro forma) on a 31% Coach gain, partly offset by a 10% Kate Spade decline; North America grew 20% and Greater China 61%. Gross margin expanded 80bps to 76.9% on operational efficiency and the Stuart Weitzman divestiture, partly offset by a 180bp tariff headwind. Non-GAAP SG&A leveraged 410bps, driving GAAP operating margin up 630bps to 22.3%. GAAP EPS rose 74% to $1.65; non-GAAP EPS rose 62% to $1.66. Cash and short-term investments were $1.07B against $2.38B of debt. Tapestry raised its FY2026 outlook for revenue, operating margin, EPS, and adjusted free cash flow, and increased planned shareholder returns to $1.6B.

drivers.explanation: Coach grew 31% (29% constant currency) on handbag unit growth over 20% and low-double-digit AUR gains; Kate Spade fell 10% constant currency. North America grew 20%, Greater China 61% (55% constant currency).
Gross margin rose 80bps to 76.9%: about 190bps of operational improvement plus a 70bp mix benefit from the Stuart Weitzman divestiture, partly offset by a 180bp tariff and duty headwind.
GAAP operating margin expanded 630bps to 22.3% on the gross-margin gain plus SG&A leverage — non-GAAP SG&A fell 410bps as a share of sales even as marketing spend rose 160bps.

GAAP EPS growth (+74%) outpaced non-GAAP EPS growth (+62%) because prior-year GAAP results carried larger comparability charges that non-GAAP excludes in both periods, narrowing the base more than the current quarter.

Broad-based outperformance and Coach momentum led Tapestry to raise FY2026 guidance for revenue, operating margin, EPS, and adjusted free cash flow, and to lift planned FY2026 shareholder returns to $1.6B from $1.5B.
